## What this is

The daemon's audit sweep used to print `append-refused … audit.sampled … was not appended (lock-timeout)` when another writer held the log, and an operator reading the daemon window took it as a lost audit record. The sample was never lost: `pendingSamples` re-derives pendency from the verified log and the next tick appends it.

- `core/audit.ts`: `TRANSIENT_APPEND_CODES` (`lock-timeout`, `head-moved`) and `isTransientAppendError`; the sweep result carries `deferred` beside `refusals`, each deferral carrying the whole candidate so the reporting layer has the action key. The list is closed in the fail-closed direction: an unknown append error code is a refusal.
- `daemon/audit.ts`: a `defer` sink; the line says the sample is NOT lost and that the sweep retries it on the next tick. The retry names itself through a bounded process-lifetime set with the standing of the existing once-per-process notice set; no append consults it.
- `daemon/daemon.ts`: warning code `sample-deferred`; the `sampled` event gains `retry?: true`, rendered by the CLI.
- AC3 decision: skip and retry at the existing 2000 ms lock wait. The tick is serial, so a longer wait delays every other step; `log advance` and `log sync` hold the lock across spans no polite wait covers, so the transient path must exist anyway; and deferring is provably lossless. Recorded in the sweep header and `docs/cli-reference.md` under `daemon run`.
- `appendSample` is untouched: it still re-reads the verified log and passes `expectedHead` (SPEC 11.1 invariants 1 and 5).
